title: €200 Billion Through One Branch: The Danske Bank Estonia Scandal, Audited
title_options: €200 Billion Through One Branch: The Danske Bank Estonia Scandal, Audited
How a Danish Bank Laundered Russia's Money and Got Fined by Washington, Not Copenhagen
Danske Bank: The Cleanest Reputation in Europe Was the Product
€200 Billion, 10,000 Customers, One Tallinn Branch: The Danske Ledger
The Biggest Money-Laundering Case in History Happened in a Nordic Bank. Nobody Went to Prison.
description:
Between 2007 and 2015 roughly €200 billion of non-resident money, much of it Russian, flowed through a single branch of Denmark's largest bank in Tallinn. A British trader warned Copenhagen in 2013. Auditors confirmed him in 2014. Nothing happened until a Danish newspaper and a law firm's report in September 2018 forced the chief executive out on live television. Then the fines came, from the United States. This is the Danske Bank Estonia ledger: Sampo Bank, Howard Wilkinson, Bruun & Hjejle, Thomas Borgen, the Estonian expulsion, the $2 billion guilty plea, and the Nordic banks that discovered they had the same problem.

▶ How this video was made
The Nordic Ledger is an independent channel. This script was researched, written and edited with human editorial judgement; AI tools were used to assist with research, drafting and production. The narration is an AI-generated voice. If you spot an error, tell us in the comments and we will pin a correction.
